description: OAuth 2.0 + OIDC + JWT decomposed. Authorization code flow, PKCE, client credentials, device code, refresh tokens. OIDC ID tokens. JWT structure, common bugs (alg=none, weak signing, missing validation). Modern patterns + pitfalls.

sub_mechanisms.name: authorization_code_flow
sub_mechanisms.definition: Client redirects to auth server; user authenticates + consents; auth server redirects back with code; client exchanges code for tokens.
sub_mechanisms.why: Most secure OAuth flow for confidential clients. Code short-lived + one-time-use. Tokens never seen by browser. Standard for server-side web apps.

sub_mechanisms.name: PKCE_proof_key
sub_mechanisms.definition: Proof Key for Code Exchange. Client generates random verifier + sends hash (challenge). Code redemption requires verifier.
sub_mechanisms.why: Mitigates code interception in public clients (mobile, SPA). Auth server returns code; only client with original verifier can exchange. Required for mobile/SPA per RFC 8252.

sub_mechanisms.name: client_credentials_flow
sub_mechanisms.definition: Machine-to-machine. Client sends client_id + client_secret; receives access token. No user.
sub_mechanisms.why: Service-to-service auth. Simpler than user flows. Client secret = static credential; rotation + storage matters.

sub_mechanisms.name: device_code_flow
sub_mechanisms.definition: Devices without browser (CLI, TV). Display code; user enters at separate device. CLI polls until approved.
sub_mechanisms.why: CLI auth (Google Cloud, GitHub CLI). Awkward UX but only secure option for headless. RFC 8628.

sub_mechanisms.name: refresh_token
sub_mechanisms.definition: Long-lived token to obtain fresh access tokens without user interaction. Used when access token expires.
sub_mechanisms.why: Access tokens short (minutes-hour); refresh long (days-permanent). User stays logged in without re-prompting. Cost: refresh token theft = persistent compromise. Rotation strategies help.

sub_mechanisms.name: scope_consent
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each authorization request specifies scopes. User consents to specific access. Resource server enforces.
sub_mechanisms.why: User-informed authorization. Granularity matters: too coarse = excessive access; too fine = consent fatigue. Industry trend toward finer scopes.

sub_mechanisms.name: OIDC_ID_token
sub_mechanisms.definition: JWT signed by auth server containing identity claims (sub, email, name). Returned alongside OAuth access token.
sub_mechanisms.why: Authentication layer over OAuth. Tells you WHO; access token tells you WHAT. SSO standard. Validate signature + issuer + audience + expiry.

sub_mechanisms.name: JWT_structure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Three base64url parts: header.payload.signature. Header: algorithm + key id. Payload: claims. Signature: over header + payload.
sub_mechanisms.why: Compact, URL-safe. Self-contained (claims travel with token). Cost: revocation hard (must check denylist or short expiry).

sub_mechanisms.name: JWT_alg_none_vulnerability
sub_mechanisms.definition: Some libraries accept JWT with alg=none (unsigned). Attacker sets header alg=none, payload anything, no signature.
sub_mechanisms.why: Famous JWT bug. Fixed in modern libraries; old versions still around. Mitigation: explicit alg validation, never trust alg from header without check.

sub_mechanisms.name: JWT_signing_algorithm_confusion
sub_mechanisms.definition: Token signed RS256 (asymmetric); verifier uses HS256 (symmetric) with public key as 'secret'. Validates incorrectly.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classic JWT bug. Library auto-selects algorithm from header. Mitigation: hardcode expected algorithm, never trust header.

sub_mechanisms.name: JWT_claim_validation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Verify iss (issuer), aud (audience), exp (expiry), nbf (not before), iat (issued at).
sub_mechanisms.why: Signature alone insufficient. Token from wrong issuer, for wrong audience, expired = invalid. Common bug: validate signature only, not claims.

sub_mechanisms.name: token_introspection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Resource server queries auth server: 'is this access token valid?' Returns active + claims.
sub_mechanisms.why: Alternative to self-validating JWT. Allows revocation. Cost: extra round trip per request. Hybrid: JWT for short-lived access + introspection for sensitive ops.

derivation_rules.name: PKCE_required_for_public_clients
if: client is public (mobile, SPA) without client secret
then: PKCE is required to prevent code interception
derivation_rules.why: Public clients can't keep secrets. PKCE proves possession via challenge/verifier pair. RFC 8252 mandates. Modern OAuth implementations enforce.

derivation_rules.name: JWT_validation_must_check_multiple_claims
if: a JWT is verified by signature only
then: it may be expired, from wrong issuer, or for different audience
derivation_rules.why: Signature proves authenticity, not currency or relevance. Library must check exp + iss + aud. Common bug: trust signature, ignore claims.

derivation_rules.name: ID_token_separate_from_access_token
derivation_rules.definition: ID token authenticates user; access token authorizes API access.
then: ID token + access token serve distinct purposes
derivation_rules.why: Don't use access token for auth (no identity claim) or ID token for API access (no authorization scope). OIDC standard split.

derivation_rules.name: refresh_token_theft_severe
then: attacker has persistent access until detected
derivation_rules.why: Refresh tokens last days-permanent. Mitigation: token rotation (each use issues new RT, old invalidates), bind to client (sender-constrained tokens), DPoP.

derivation_rules.name: JWT_revocation_inherently_hard
then: revoking before expiry requires denylist or introspection
derivation_rules.why: Server has no state. Mitigation: short expiry (5-15 min) + refresh token rotation; or introspection (heavy); or token denylist (state). Trade-offs per application.
